page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, presenting 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per core. Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring attached cloud storage volumes for persistent data. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the entry-level compute capacity of a single physical core alongside its dedicated memory allocation. Single-core performance demonstrates moderate throughput, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 1264.0. However, multi-core capacity is restrained by the dual-thread topology on one core, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 1594.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2789.36. Memory bandwidth testing shows read throughput of 21.94 GB/s and write throughput of 14.89 GB/s on large uncached blocks. In application benchmarks, the server delivers 1.75 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.0 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

The ecs.r6a.large is structured for workloads prioritizing memory capacity over intensive compute parallelism. It is appropriate for small in-memory data stores, caching layers, lightweight relational databases, and background services that require a 16 GB memory footprint without demanding substantial multi-core calculation speeds.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It does not include local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating entirely with remote block storage for persistence. Performance metrics reflect its compact core allocation, showing moderate single-thread execution with a Geekbench single-core score of 1264.0, balanced by a lower multi-core capacity with a Geekbench score of 1594.0 and 1.75 million Redis SET operations per second. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, the ecs.r6a.large is designed for memory-intensive entry-level workloads, including small caching tiers, microservices requiring sizable memory footprints, and low-concurrency database systems.
